def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    path = "data/legal/input/csn-data-book-2024-csv/CSVs/2024_CSN_State_Top_Ten_Report_Categories.csv"

    # Row 0: title; Row 1: blank; Row 2: actual header
    df = pd.read_csv(path, header=2)

    # Drop any blank/footer rows
    df = df.dropna(subset=["State", "Category"]).copy()

    # Clean numeric fields
    df["# of Reports"] = (
        df["# of Reports"].astype(str).str.replace(",", "", regex=False)
    )
    df["# of Reports"] = pd.to_numeric(df["# of Reports"], errors="coerce")

    df["Percentage"] = df["Percentage"].astype(str).str.replace("%", "", regex=False)
    df["Percentage"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Percentage"], errors="coerce")

    # Standardize column names
    df = df.rename(columns={"# of Reports": "numReports", "Percentage": "percentage"})

    return df

def process(topTenCategories) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = topTenCategories.copy()

    # Determine "top" as the highest % share within each state (ties allowed)
    df["rankPct"] = df.groupby("State")["percentage"].rank(method="min", ascending=False)

    out = df[(df["Category"] == "Identity Theft") & (df["rankPct"] == 1)].copy()

    # Return unique states (sorted) where Identity Theft is a top category
    out = (
        out[["State"]]
        .drop_duplicates()
        .sort_values("State")
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

    return out
